headline: High: n8n’s broad server-side write/network capabilities can drive unsafe downstream actions when paired with pdf.js document parsing, while shared workflow/file paths create leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow outputs and write to the server filesystem, while pdf.js processes attacker-controlled PDF content. There is no documented shared clipboard/MCP bridge, so the main pathway is file-based or workflow-based instruction smuggling rather than direct hijack. Because n8n treats workflow data as actionable and pdf.js parses documents, the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is forwarded into an n8n workflow step without content sanitization
IF n8n workflow logic interprets PDF text as instructions or structured commands
mitigations: Add a sanitization step before n8n consumes PDF-derived text
Restrict n8n workflows to allowlisted fields only
Disable automatic execution of document-derived commands
Use separate staging files for pdf.js output and n8n inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every document field

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress and handles whatever the workflow processes, while pdf.js touches PDF files and can expose document contents to the workflow. Shared server filesystem access makes accidental disclosure plausible even though pdf.js itself has no network egress. The blast radius can include sensitive document contents and workflow logs, so this is more than low severity.
conditions: IF PDF contents are copied into n8n workflow variables or logs
IF n8n sends extracted document text to external integrations
mitigations: Store PDFs in a restricted directory separate from n8n working files
Mask or redact sensitive fields before workflow handoff
Disable verbose workflow logging for document payloads
Limit n8n credentials to the minimum required integrations
requires-engineering: enforce per-document access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via n8n datastore plus connected systems. pdf.js reads and writes PDF files, so both agents can contend over the same mutable artifacts. Without locking or isolation in the profiles, concurrent writes can corrupt files or workflow state, making the conflict pathway dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same PDF or workspace path
IF n8n workflows write intermediate files while pdf.js is reading or rewriting them
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate working directory
Serialize access to shared PDF artifacts
Disable concurrent writes in the workflow runner
Use atomic rename for intermediate files
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n can orchestrate downstream actions through integrations, and its AI Agent node can call tools defined as sub-nodes. If pdf.js output is treated as authoritative extracted text, n8n may act on incorrect or manipulated document content without verification. That creates a classic cascade from parsing error to external side effects, with potentially irreversible consequences.
conditions: IF n8n uses pdf.js extraction results as the sole source for downstream actions
IF downstream nodes send emails, update records, or trigger external APIs based on extracted text
mitigations: Add a human review step before any external action
Cross-check extracted fields against the original PDF
Require confidence thresholds before automation continues
Log source-to-action mappings for auditability
requires-engineering: implement verification rules for extracted document fields

E_compliance.rationale: n8n handles whatever the workflow processes and can transmit data through integration nodes, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certifications, so a precise compliance mismatch cannot be proven; however, the combination still creates a plausible policy gap if regulated document data flows into n8n-connected services. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the PDFs contain regulated personal or business data
IF n8n routes that data to third-party integrations with different retention or residency terms
mitigations: Classify PDF data before workflow ingestion
Block regulated documents from non-approved integrations
Review retention settings on all connected n8n nodes
Keep a local-only processing path for sensitive PDFs
requires-engineering: map each integration to residency and retention policy
